# Analyze the relationship between introduction pathways and mrt in invasion_success dataset
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Check the distribution of mrt across different introduction pathways
sns.boxplot(x='intro.pathway', y='mrt', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Distribution of Minimum Residence Time (mrt) by Introduction Pathway')
plt.xlabel('Introduction Pathway')
plt.ylabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.show()

# Check for statistical significance using ANOVA
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
filtered_data = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group data by 'intro.pathway' and extract mrt values
groups = filtered_data.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].apply(list)

# Perform ANOVA
f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*groups)
f_statistic, p_value

# Analyze the relationship between mrt, introduction pathways, and invasion success (number.of.invaded.plots)
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between mrt and intro.pathway on number.of.invaded.plots
model = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ mrt * intro.pathway', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

# Check for missing values in the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success.isnull().sum()

# Perform separate linear regression for each introduction pathway
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Define the response variable
y = invasion_success['number.of.invaded.plots']

# Define the predictor variable
X = sm.add_constant(invasion_success['mrt'])

# Fit the model for each pathway
pathways = invasion_success['intro.pathway'].unique()

results = {}
for pathway in pathways:
    subset = invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]
    X_subset = sm.add_constant(subset['mrt'])
    model = sm.OLS(y, X_subset).fit()
    results[pathway] = model

results
